next.name: Threat Group-3390
next.headline: Threat Group-3390: a long-running group known by many names, with a wide malware kit
next.in_short: Threat Group-3390 is tracked as APT27, Iron Tiger, Emissary Panda and more. Reports on file link it to tools like HyperBro and PlugX, a web-shell and downloader trail, and a chat-app campaign aimed at three operating systems.

sentences.t: Threat Group-3390 is also tracked as Earth Smilodon, TG-3390, Emissary Panda, BRONZE UNION, APT27, Iron Tiger, LuckyMouse and Linen Typhoon.
Google Threat Intelligence Group describes APT27 as a PRC-nexus threat actor and says it observed APT27-associated activity that used Gemini.
The catalogue lists many tools for the group, including PlugX, HyperBro, China Chopper, Cobalt Strike, Mimikatz, Impacket and gh0st RAT.
Recorded Future's Insikt Group says LuckyMouse (TG-3390, Emissary Panda, Bronze Union) is among the actors that have historically used Scanbox, a reconnaissance framework that can log keystrokes.
One analyst's report says the Redosdru downloader is commonly associated with APT27/Iron Tiger. The report says Microsoft reported it as early as July 2009.
The Malpedia page for the TwoFace web shell lists APT27 among five associated actors. According to Unit 42, TwoFace has two stages, a loader and a payload, and is written in C#.
A report titled "Iron Tiger Compromises Chat Application Mimi, Targets Windows, Mac, and Linux Users" lists indicators for HyperBro samples on Windows and Rshell samples on Linux and Mac OS.
Google's report says an APT27 fleet management application is likely to support an ORB network. The report was published on 2026-05-11.
Defenders can use the published indicator lists and tool names to check their own systems for signs of this group.
